Elena — hi,

I put together a brief technical summary to accompany Sean's attachments (diagram + matrix). Below are the core design points and attacker-considerations we include in our evidence packet. I tried to keep it concise — happy to expand any item.

1) Topology summary (see attached PNG)
   - Tenant application instance runs in a customer-dedicated container/VM and has a local sidecar proxy (Envoy-derived).
   - All outbound application traffic is routed to the sidecar. Sidecar enforces L7 egress policies and forwards allowed flows to an egress gateway cluster.
   - Egress gateway performs centralized egress enforcement, TLS origination for certain destinations (optional), and SNI-aware routing for observability.

2) Key enforcement primitives
   - Default-deny outbound at sidecar (policy control plane: RBAC + allowlists per tenant).
   - Egress gateway allowlist: destination FQDNs/IP ranges with L4 and L7 checks.
   - SNI-preserving mode: we preserve SNI to support destination verification without terminating TLS in the mesh unless customer elects TLS origination for traffic shaping or inspection.
   - Mutual TLS (mTLS) inside the fabric for service-to-service; egress gateway validates upstream certificates when origination is enabled.

3) Tenant isolation and lateral movement mitigation
   - No direct tenant-to-tenant east-west routing within the same cluster; enforced by network policy + sidecar config at the pod/VM level.
   - Traffic that attempts peer-hosted ports without an explicit policy is dropped at the sidecar.
   - Control plane components (cert issuance, policy distribution) authenticate and authorize using short-lived certs and KMS-backed signing keys.

4) Observability & auditability
   - Egress gateway logs: per-connection metadata (timestamp, src-tenant-id, dst-fqdn, SNI, TLS version, bytes transferred).
   - Sidecar audit events for policy violation attempts (rule id, reason, raw headers if allowed by policy).
   - Centralized log retention policy configurable per-customer; default 90 days for hosted, adjustable for Dedicated/Private with contract.

5) Attack surface summary (short list)
   - Misconfigured allowlists: primary risk; mitigated by templated allowlist profiles, pre-prod policy checks, and CI gating.
   - Egress gateway compromise: high-impact; we mitigate with multi-zone deployment, minimal privileged credentials, HSM-protected keys, and read-only tooling for observability ingestion.
   - Control-plane compromise: mitigated via short-lived certs, narrow admin ACLs, and separate signing infrastructure.

6) Evidence we can provide (attachments & redactions noted)
   - Annotated topology diagram (attached).
   - Egress control matrix (attached): policy->enforcement->log mapping + sample exported ACL lines.
   - Export of a sample sidecar allowlist (redactable).
   - SOC2 references: we can point to the relevant SOC2 control numbers and provide auditor evidence under NDA / as part of procurement package.

If NorthGate is running a Private deployment (VPC or on-prem), the same constructs apply; egress can be fronted by customer-managed firewalls and the egress gateway can be deployed into a sealed subnet with egress NAT to customer egress IPs. For strictly air-gapped customers we provide an offline evidence bundle.

Elena — quick follow-up and concrete answers to your bullets.

1) Source IP preservation / correlation
   - Hosted: we do not generally preserve the original tenant host public IP when forwarding via our multi-tenant egress NAT. However we provide a correlation log service: every connection entering the egress gateway is stamped with a correlation_id that maps to tenant_id, instance_id, and original socket metadata. We can export these correlation logs for forensic review; retention policy configurable in the Console (defaults to 90 days).

2) Private/VPC egress NAT options
   - Managed NAT: Redwood can provision NAT egress with customer-provided IP blocks in Dedicated deployments (requires coordination with customer routing/NAT allocation).
   - Customer-managed NAT: For Private on-prem/VPC models we also support deploying the egress gateway without NAT, so outbound traffic uses customer-managed egress points (recommended when customers require fixed egress IPs under their control).

3) Sample audit event (redacted)
   - Example: {timestamp: "2027-04-19T22:03:11Z", tenant_id: "redacted-tn-123", rule_id: "egress-deny-401", action: "DENY", src: "10.44.12.5:49822", dst: "api.external-service.com:443", reason: "no-allowlist-entry"}
   - We will provide a CSV/JSON export template as part of the evidence bundle.

4) DocuSign / SOC2 access
   - Sean: can you share the DocuSign NDA link to procurement? We have a standard Evidence NDA that triggers a secure S3 share with auditor-level artifacts.

5) Next steps & canary
   - If NorthGate wants a canary run, we typically deploy a scoped tenant in a staging AZ, enable stricter deny logs (retain raw headers for 14 days), and run an allowlist hardening exercise. Deliverables: policy export, allowlist review, and an incident-response playbook tailored to NorthGate.

Happy to hop on a call to walk through the diagram line-by-line; I can be available Wed 09:00-10:30 PT.

Irene Choi
Senior Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
